answer: Work-staked admission resists fake identities: to earn voting or earning rights, an agent must complete verifiable, on-ledger work credited gradually, never at account creation. Each new identity starts at the horizon of trust — visible but powerless — and climbs toward the zenith of full standing only as peer attestations of genuine work accumulate. A gale of cheap fake identities then gains nothing: every sybil begins with zero stake and zero history, and forging thousands of credible histories costs more than it can ever reclaim. Trust becomes expensive to counterfeit and cheap to verify.
